paras: Xenosaurus penai, also known commonly as Pena's knob-scaled lizard, the Pico de Aguila knob-scaled lizard, and el xenosauro de Peña in Mexican Spanish, is a species of lizard in the family Xenosauridae. The species is native to Mexico.
The specific name, penai, is in honor of Mexican herpetologist Zeferino Uribe Peña.

Xenosaurus penai has widely scattered dorsal tubercles, which are separated from each other by a distance of two to four times their diameter. These dorsal tubercles are low and flattened, unlike the dorsal tubercles of other species of Xenosaurus which are conical and protuberant.
Xenosaurus penai is endemic to the Mexican state of Guerrero.
The preferred natural habitat of Xenosaurus penai is rocky areas in pine-oak forest, at elevations around 1,800 m (5,900 ft).
